items.summary: AWS Marketplace now supports agentic payments over the x402 protocol, so AI agents can discover and buy select products and pay per request in US dollars through AgentCore payments, part of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Agents often need paid APIs, data, or content mid-task, but access usually requires a person to sign up, add a payment method, and create an API key. With agentic payments, customers skip that per-seller setup, and charges settle on their existing AWS bill with no crypto wallet required. Customers enable the AWS Marketplace payment connector in AgentCore payments, then they or their agents find listings through the AWS Marketplace connector in AgentCore Gateway. For example, a re
lines: AWS Marketplace now supports agentic payments over the x402 protocol, so AI agents can discover and buy select products.
Agents pay per request in US dollars through AgentCore payments, part of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
Charges settle on the existing AWS bill, and no crypto wallet is required.
Customers enable the AWS Marketplace payment connector in AgentCore payments, then find listings through the connector in AgentCore Gateway.

items.headline: AWS Lambda durable functions now supports OpenTelemetry tracing
items.summary: AWS Lambda announces OpenTelemetry (OTel) support for Lambda durable functions. You can now trace your durable executions and emit traces to Amazon CloudWatch and other industry-standard observability tools. This helps you find bottlenecks in your system, root cause failures faster, and understand how your workflows behave in production. With Lambda durable functions, you can build resilient, multi-step applications and AI workflows that run for up to one year, with built-in checkpointing and automatic retries. Durable functions can run for hours, or days, suspending and resuming across many Lambda invocations. The new OpenTelemetry plugin emits a unified trace that spans a full durable exec
lines: AWS Lambda now supports OpenTelemetry (OTel) tracing for Lambda durable functions.
Traces can be sent to Amazon CloudWatch and other industry-standard observability tools.
Durable functions can run for up to one year, with built-in checkpointing and automatic retries.
Teams can use the traces to find bottlenecks and root-cause failures in multi-step workflows in production.

items.headline: Amazon Route 53 now supports health checks for private endpoints
items.summary: Amazon Route 53 now offers Private Endpoint Health Checks, enabling business-critical workloads that never touch the public internet, such as internal APIs, databases, and self-hosted nodes behind internal load balancers or in private subnets, to use native health monitoring and automatic DNS failover. Customers can health-check any reachable private target by IP address, domain, or port over HTTP, HTTPS, or TCP. Customers can associate these health checks with Route 53 DNS records across routing policies in private hosted zones, so Route 53 routes traffic only to healthy endpoints and manages failover automatically. Previously, teams built custom control loops using Amazon CloudWatch alarms
lines: Amazon Route 53 now offers Private Endpoint Health Checks for workloads that do not use the public internet.
Health checks can target a private IP address, domain, or port over HTTP, HTTPS, or TCP.
Route 53 can associate these health checks with DNS records in private hosted zones, routing traffic only to healthy endpoints.
Teams can use native health monitoring and automatic DNS failover instead of building custom control loops with CloudWatch alarms.

items.headline: AWS Lambda now supports a 30-minute timeout for on-demand Event Functions
items.summary: AWS Lambda now supports a 30-minute function timeout for Event Functions that run on demand, doubling the 15-minute limit for synchronous , asynchronous , and event source mapping (ESM) invocations. On Lambda Managed Instances , synchronous invocations also support up to 30 minutes, while asynchronous and ESM invocations keep the 90-minute timeout launched in September 2026. You can now run long-running workloads such as AI inference, media transcoding, and financial calculations for spiky or steady-state traffic without re-architecting your applications. Customers use Event Functions to build event-driven processors, API backends, and data pipelines. By default, Event Functions run on deman
lines: AWS Lambda now supports a 30-minute function timeout for on-demand Event Functions, up from the 15-minute limit.
On Lambda Managed Instances, synchronous invocations also support up to 30 minutes, while asynchronous and ESM invocations keep the 90-minute timeout launched in September 2026.
Teams can run long workloads such as AI inference, media transcoding, and financial calculations without re-architecting their applications.

items.headline: AWS Elemental MediaTailor adds Dynamic Avail Sizing for live HLS
items.summary: AWS Elemental MediaTailor now supports Dynamic Avail Sizing, which reduces the slate viewers see when ad breaks, also called avails, in live HLS streams go unfilled. MediaTailor is a server-side ad insertion and channel assembly service that personalizes ads in live and on-demand video streams. When the ad decision server returns fewer ads than a break allows, dynamic avail sizing omits the unfilled time and resumes programming early instead of showing slate. To keep playback continuous, MediaTailor holds back a configurable reserve of content behind the live edge and draws on it when a break ends early. When the reserve runs low, MediaTailor requests extra ad time in later breaks to refill
lines: AWS Elemental MediaTailor now supports Dynamic Avail Sizing for live HLS streams.
When fewer ads are returned than a break allows, the unfilled time is omitted and programming resumes early instead of showing slate.
A configurable reserve of content behind the live edge keeps playback continuous, and extra ad time is requested in later breaks when the reserve runs low.

items.headline: Amazon Cognito now supports AWS Secrets Manager for app client secrets
items.summary: Amazon Cognito now integrates with AWS Secrets Manager , so you can store and manage your user pool app client secrets in Secrets Manager. Amazon Cognito helps you implement secure sign-in and access control for users, AI agents, and microservices in minutes. An app client secret authenticates your application to Cognito. Previously, you had to manage and rotate these secrets in Cognito directly. With this integration, you can leverage Secrets Manager for capabilities including rotation, access control with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies, and encryption with an AWS managed key or your own AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. This can help with periodi
lines: Amazon Cognito now integrates with AWS Secrets Manager, so user pool app client secrets can be stored and managed there.
Previously, these secrets were managed and rotated directly in Cognito.
Secrets Manager adds rotation, access control with IAM policies, and encryption with an AWS managed key or a customer managed AWS KMS key.

items.headline: ThreatsDay: GPT-6.2 Jailbreak Flaws, BubbleLoader PNG Malware, $500M Ransom Demands + 17 More Stories
items.summary: The easiest way to fool someone is to give them something they already expect. A job offer. A message about a service outage. A familiar app. Nothing looks strange at first. And that's the problem. This week's stories show how ordinary things are being used to steal data, spread malware, and get people to hand over access. There's another shift worth watching. AI is making some attacks easier
lines: Reported by The Hacker News: This weekly roundup covers GPT-6.2 jailbreak flaws, BubbleLoader PNG malware, and $500M ransom demands, plus 17 more stories.
The roundup says attackers are using ordinary things, such as job offers and service outage messages, to steal data, spread malware, and gain access.

lines: Reported by The Hacker News: Threat actors are exploiting a recently disclosed critical flaw in Cisco Expressway to breach a Russian organization shortly after a proof-of-concept exploit was publicly released.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-123890 (CVSS score: 9.8), is a case of authentication bypass in the VMware Directory Service that could be exploited to gain unauthorized

items.headline: Linux KVM Flaw CVE-2026-99312 Lets Guest VMs Access Host Memory on AMD Hosts
items.summary: A flaw in KVM, the hypervisor built into the Linux kernel, let researchers read about 127 GB of a cloud server's memory from inside a virtual machine of their own on DigitalOcean. On a shared server, that memory can include other customers' virtual machines. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-99312, affects only hosts with AMD processors and nested virtualization enabled. Fixed kernels shipped
lines: Reported by The Hacker News: Researchers used a flaw in KVM, the hypervisor built into the Linux kernel, to read about 127 GB of a cloud server's memory from a virtual machine of their own on DigitalOcean.
The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-99312, affects only hosts with AMD processors and nested virtualization enabled.
On shared servers, that memory can include other customers' virtual machines, so IT teams running affected AMD hosts have a reason to check their exposure.
